text:
Alex: Quick proposal — introduce an 'interrupt-pivot' path in the runtime so in-flight streaming requests can be gracefully handed off when a preemptible node gets a termination notice. Goal: avoid dropped responses and reduce client-side resume complexity.

Maria: Sounds useful. A couple Qs: how do we guarantee token continuity so clients can stitch partial streams without duplication? and what about metric attribution / billing? :thinking_face:

Jamal: Is this basically an extra network hop (handoff) on termination? Concerned about added latency and hotspots. Also what happens for requests that have already filled KV cache / are mid-generation?

Priya: Sketch of behavior I had in mind:
1) Node receives termination notice (cloud preemptible notice).
2) Runtime enters graceful window (configurable, e.g. grace_ms = 30_000) and attempts to finish short requests.
3) For long-running streams, runtime emits an opaque resume token representing the partial response + generator state, and forwards the stream to a warm standby or a lightweight handoff endpoint.
4) Client is given a final partial chunk and a resume token header (X-Resume-Token). Client can immediately re-open the stream with the resume token and continue from the last emitted token.

This avoids client needing to diff responses and lets us keep dedupe logic server-side. We also need a requeue fallback if handoff fails (enqueue with prefer-warm policy).

Jamal: Ok. We should cap number of requeues and handoffs per request to avoid thundering replays. Also prefer a warm-standby in the same region/shard to minimize KV/cache rebuild.

Alex: Config prototype (runtime-level):

```yaml
interrupt_pivot:
  enabled: true
  grace_ms: 30000
  max_handoffs: 2
  handoff_endpoint: "tcp://handoff.int-pool.internal:12000"
  resume_header: "X-Resume-Token"
  requeue_policy: "prefer-warm, then-queue, then-dedicated"
  dedupe_window_ms: 10000
```

Maria: Important: metrics and billing. If a request is handed off we must not double-count tokens when both source and target emit overlapping chunks. We need a single request id that both sides log and a dedupe marker on metrics. Also add a trace/span that links both RPCs.

Priya: Client-side example for SDK resume flow:

```http
POST /v1/stream
Host: api.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: text/event-stream

# initial request
{ "model": "rwd-2-large", "prompt": "..." }

# server returns partial stream, then final chunk with header:
X-Resume-Token: rtok-abc123

# client resumes
GET /v1/stream?resume=true
X-Resume-Token: rtok-abc123
```

Jamal: We should also consider a graceful CPU/GPU reclaim: try to checkpoint minimal generation state (rng, kv pointers, position) rather than full weights. That keeps handoff light. If we can't checkpoint (e.g., unsupported model), route to requeue instead.

Alex: For observability: add these fields to logs: interrupt_reason, resume_token_hash, handoff_target, handoff_latency, requeue_count. Maria will own dashboard + alert for handoff failure rate > 2%.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-2743 — "interrupt-pivot: design doc + perf bench" and attached initial sketch. Assignees: jamal, priya, maria.

Maria: Thx infra-bot. I'll add metrics spec and billing rules (single-request attribution, dedupe marker).

Jamal: Plan for implementation:
- runtime: accept handshake to send minimal state to handoff endpoint 
- handoff pool: lightweight process that rehydrates stream and resumes generation 
- queue fallback: ensure enqueue preserves resume token semantics
Target: RFD + perf run in 2 weeks.

Priya: SDK changes: expose resume token to callers, provide high-level auto-resume toggle (off by default), and add tests for duplicate suppression. I'll prototype JS + Python.

Alex: Action items:
- Alex: write short design doc + perf plan (RFD link in INF-2743) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
- Jamal: runtime PR + unit tests for interrupt handshake and handoff (assign to eng-runtime)
- Priya: SDK resume support + tests
- Maria: metrics, billing rules, and dashboard; alert on handoff errors > 2%

Alex: Anyone object to rolling this out behind a flag and running a controlled perf test on staging with some synthetic long streams? If all good we can enable for a subset of spot pools. :white_check_mark:

Jamal: No objections. Prefer gradual rollout to a single region and dedicated warm-standby pool first.

Priya: Agreed. Will start SDK PR after design doc.

Maria: I'll pair with Jamal on metric naming to avoid surprises.

Alex: Great — I'll post the RFD to INF-2743 in ~1d and include a proposed experimental matrix and perf goals. Thanks all.
